items.hint: Look for two numbers whose product is the constant term and whose sum is the middle coefficient, sign included.
worked: Since the leading coefficient is $1$, find two numbers with product $20$ and sum $-9$.
A positive product with a negative sum forces BOTH numbers negative: $-4$ and $-5$.

items.stem: A student factors $-x^{2}+5x+6$ in two steps. Step 1: $-x^{2}+5x+6=-(x^{2}+5x+6)$. Step 2: $-(x^{2}+5x+6)=-(x+2)(x+3)$. Which choice names the first error and gives the correct complete factorization?
items.hint: Multiply each candidate answer back out and see which one reproduces $-x^{2}+5x+6$ exactly.
worked: Pulling out $-1$ changes the sign of EVERY term: $-x^{2}+5x+6=-(x^{2}-5x-6)$, so Step 1 is already wrong.
Inside, two numbers with product $-6$ and sum $-5$ are $-6$ and $1$, giving $x^{2}-5x-6=(x-6)(x+1)$.
Check: $(x-6)(x+1)=x^{2}-5x-6$, and the outside $-1$ makes it $-x^{2}+5x+6$.

options.text: Step 2 is the first error, because $x^{2}+5x+6=(x+1)(x+6)$.
Step 1 is the first error; it should read $-(x^{2}-5x-6)$, so the factorization is $-(x-6)(x+1)$.
Neither step contains an error, so the factorization is $-(x+2)(x+3)$.
Step 1 is unnecessary, because $-x^{2}$ is the same as $(-x)^{2}$; the factorization is $(x+2)(x+3)$.

items.stem: Exactly one of the four statements below is true. Which one?
items.hint: Expand each right-hand side and compare it term by term with the left-hand side; a missing middle term is still a mismatch.
worked: Factoring $3$ out of $3x^{2}+6x-9$ must divide EVERY term: $3(x^{2}+2x-3)$, not $3(x^{2}+6x-9)$.
$(2x+2)(x+3)=2x^{2}+8x+6$, so it is not $2x^{2}+7x+6$; the correct split is $(2x+3)(x+2)$.
$(3x+1)(2x-3)=6x^{2}-9x+2x-3=6x^{2}-7x-3$, which matches, so that statement is the true one.
